_comment: Causal study design parameters for DTI benchmark contamination paper.

estimand.name: Average Treatment Effect of Pretraining Corpus Contamination
estimand.control_unit: DeepDTA (trained from scratch, no pretrained components)

holdout_arm.rationale: Compounds deposited after all three pretraining corpus cutoffs (ESM-2 Apr 2021, ChemBERTa Jun 2020, MolBERT Nov 2020), structurally novel vs the MolBERT pretraining corpus.

parallel_trends.description: DeepDTA's benchmark-vs-holdout Pearson r gap is attributable only to dataset difficulty differences, not pretraining contamination (it has none). Verified by checking that DeepDTA's gap is near zero.
parallel_trends.falsification_test: If DeepDTA shows a large gap, holdout difficulty is confounded — DiD is not identified.

stable_unit_treatment.description: ESM-2 performance on one compound does not affect performance on another. Satisfied by pair-level independence in the MLP probe architecture.

no_spillover.description: Holdout compounds are genuinely novel vs ChEMBL27 (max Tanimoto < 0.4). Spillover channel is structural: if holdout compounds were similar to training compounds, any advantage ESM-2 shows would be contamination, not a threat — it would underestimate DiD.

secondary.interpretation: Negative rho = higher contamination -> smaller error -> inflated scores (continuous dose-response)

robustness.interpretation: ESM-2 should show larger r_contaminated vs r_clean gap than DeepDTA; supports DiD parallel trends
